title: Lipid droplets buffer hydrogen sulfide-induced redox imbalance.
abstract: The electron transport chain is a signaling hub for hydrogen sulfide (H2S) that serves both as a respiratory substrate and an inhibitor. While acute sulfide toxicity is well characterized, cellular adaptations to chronic H2S, particularly microbially-derived sulfide exposure in colon, is poorly understood. We report that chronic, low-level H2S exposure (4 to 20 µM) drives robust carbon sequestration in lipid droplets (LD) across several human cell lines, driven by a coordinated remodeling of red
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Polysaccharide A1 from Bran-Fried Atractylodes lancea Regulates Cyclophosphamide-induced Intestinal Immune Injury in Mice via the Faecalibaculum rodentium-Mediated IAA-AHR/RORC Axis.
abstract: Cyclophosphamide-induced intestinal injury is often characterized by gut microbiota dysbiosis and metabolite imbalance. Bran-fried Atractylodes lancea polysaccharide (FALP-A1) protects against cyclophosphamide-induced intestinal injury by significantly modulating Faecalibaculum rodentium abundance. However, the mechanism of FALP-A1-mediated F. rodentium regulation remains unclear. journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry

title: Acetate modulates host physiology and bacterial energetics to improve antibiotic efficacy during obesity-associated infection.
abstract: Antibiotic efficacy is conventionally attributed to the susceptibility of the infecting pathogen. However, obese patients experience disproportionately poor infection outcomes despite receiving antibiotics to which pathogens remain genetically susceptible. These observations suggest that host-associated factors can influence treatment outcomes independently of the bacterial genotype, although the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. title: l-Arginine Ameliorates IBS-D by Modulating the Ligilactobacillus murinus-LCA-FXR/eNOS Signaling Axis.
abstract: l-Arginine is a semiessential amino acid with diverse metabolic functions and has been implicated in gastrointestinal health through interactions with the gut microbiota; however, its therapeutic potential in diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-D) remains unclear. Here, an IBS-D mouse model was established in C57BL/6J mice, and multiomics analyses combined with in vivo and in vitro validation were performed to investigate the mechanisms underlying l-arginine-mediated protection. l
journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry

title: Gut microbiota modulates hyodeoxycholic acid to inhibit leukemia development.
abstract: To explore the role of gut microbiota and bile acid (BA) metabolism in acute myeloid leukemia (AML), we analyzed samples from 29 patients via 16S rDNA sequencing and LC-QTOF-MS, and performed functional studies on Enterococcus faecalis and hyodeoxycholic acid (HDCA). Results revealed a dynamic shift in gut microbiota diversity during treatment, which recovered after therapy. title: Polyamine depletion inhibits murine and human norovirus infection.
abstract: Noroviruses are non-enveloped, positive-sense RNA viruses in the family Caliciviridae. Human noroviruses (HNoVs) are the leading cause of viral gastrointestinal disease. Despite their clinical relevance, therapeutic strategies for norovirus infections remain limited, partly due to challenges in cultivating HNoV and limited understanding of virus-host interactions. Polyamines (PAs) are small polycationic metabolites derived from amino acid metabolism that are essential for diverse cellular functi

title: Natural Glycosides in Neurodegenerative Diseases: Multi-Target Mechanisms via the Gut-Brain Axis.
abstract: The multifactorial complexity of neurodegenerative diseases (NDs), including Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease, limits the efficacy of single-target therapies. Natural glycosides exhibit promising neuroprotective potential, but their clinical translation is hindered by poor oral bioavailability and limited blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration. title: Synbiotic of 2'-FL and B. longum subsp. infantis BXY2 Alleviates Colitis in Toddler Microbiota-Associated Mice: Potential Involvement of Gut Microbial Arachidonic Acid Metabolism.
abstract: Increasing inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) incidence in toddlers requires safe interventions. We developed a synbiotic combining 2'-fucosyllactose (2'-FL) with Bifidobacterium strain and evaluated its protective efficacy against DSS-induced colitis in toddler microbiota-associated (TMA) mice. Among 30 Bifidobacterium strains, Bifidobacterium longum subsp. infantis BXY2 and Bifidobacterium. breve BG4 utilized 2'-FL in vitro. journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry

title: Azelaic Acid Mediates the Protective Effect of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum F1m against Colitis via PPARγ Activation.
abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic inflammatory bowel disease with a high recurrence risk. Although probiotics show promise for UC treatment, the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Herein, we found that Lactiplantibacillus plantarum F1m, isolated from yak yogurt, alleviated dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis in mice, improving symptoms, restoring intestinal barrier function, and alleviating gut microbiota dysbiosis. title: Functional methylthio-alkane reductases are widely distributed for bacterial organic sulfur acquisition.
abstract: Methylthio-alkane reductase (MAR) is a relative of nitrogenase that cleaves methylthio-alkanes for methanethiol liberation and subsequent methionine biogenesis. For example, dimethylsulfide, the most abundant volatile organic sulfur compound, is cleaved to methanethiol and methane. To date, the only verified MAR enzymes are from Alphaproteobacteria like Rhodospirillum rubrum, despite the long-time observation of gene homologs with potential MAR function present across diverse taxa. title: Colon-targeted EGCG delivery remodels the gut microenvironment to enhance therapeutic efficacy in ulcerative colitis.
abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic intestinal inflammatory disorder characterized by epithelial barrier disruption, oxidative stress, and gut microbiota dysbiosis. Although epigallocatechin-3-gallate (EGCG) exhibits potent anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities, its clinical application is limited by poor stability and low colonic bioavailability. Herein, EGCG-loaded Eudragit® S100-coated chitosan microparticles (EG@euCS MPs) were developed as a colon-targeted oral delivery platforms int
journal: Journal of controlled release : official journal of the Controlled Release Society

title: Akkermansia muciniphila attenuates anti-tuberculosis drug-induced liver injury through gut-liver axis by promoting Nr4a1 transcription.
abstract: Drug-induced liver injury (DILI) is a frequent adverse event associated with anti-tuberculosis therapy, and current clinical management options remain limited. Given the pivotal role of the gut-liver axis in liver pathophysiology, this study investigated the potential and underlying roles of Akkermansia muciniphila (A.muc) in ameliorating anti-tuberculosis drug-induced liver injury (ADLI). A reduction in the abundance of A. muc was observed during ADLI progression, suggesting its possible involv

title: Microbiota-derived SCFAs modulate Socs36E-mediated feedback to regulate intestinal stem cell proliferation upon Atg4 loss in Drosophila.
abstract: Microbial metabolites affect host physiology, but how they link genetic defects to abnormal stem cell behavior is unclear. In Drosophila, losing Atg4 in progenitors changes the gut microbiota and raises short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), such as acetate and propionate. These SCFAs increase intracellular acetyl-CoA, which boosts acetylation by inhibiting histone deacetylases (HDACs) and activating multiple histone acetyltransferases. Chromatin immunoprecipitation identifies Socs36E as a direct acet

title: Hierarchical analysis of metabolic phenotype reveals distinct microbiota and circulatory transcriptome in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.
abstract: To investigate how visceral adiposity and insulin resistance, defined respectively by visceral adiposity index (VAI) and triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index, jointly influence gut microbiota composition and immune transcriptomes in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), and to explore potential mechanistic pathways.

title: A Hyaluronic Acid-Stabilized Zinc-Loaded Probiotic Mitigates Nanoplastic Toxicity across the Microbiota-Gut-Brain Axis.
abstract: Nanoplastics are emerging stressors that perturb host physiology across the gut-immune-brain continuum, yet scalable interventions remain limited. Here, we engineer ZG@EcN@HA, a biohybrid living system created by vacuum-assisted intracellular loading of zinc gluconate into Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 (EcN) followed by an outer hyaluronic acid (HA) shell. This architecture preserves probiotic culturability under gastric challenge and supports sustained zinc availability in intestinal conditions.

title: The Gut-Brain Axis in Binge Eating Disorder: From Pathophysiological Mechanisms to Emerging Therapeutic Targets.
abstract: Binge-eating disorder (BED) is one of the most prevalent eating disorders worldwide; however, current pharmacological and psychological interventions provide limited long-term efficacy. Increasing evidence indicates that dysregulation of the gut-brain axis (GBA) via altered gut microbiota, impaired hormonal signaling, vagal dysfunction, and HPA axis hyperactivity disrupts energy homeostasis and feeding regulation in BED. title: Mechanistic role of functional bacterial amyloids (FuBAs) in inflammatory responses, ubiquitin proteasome system (UPS) impairment, and cross-seedings with host amyloids.
abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases are characterized by disruption of protein homeostasis, aggregation, inflammation, and neuronal resilience, with age affecting disease susceptibility. Bacterial amyloids, such as curli, Fap, TasA, and phenol-soluble modulins, are functional amyloids that aid in biofilm formation and potentially interact with host proteins and innate immune pathways. title: An antibiotic-treated mouse model reveals the progression of intestinal botulism.
abstract: Intestinal botulism, including infant botulism and adult intestinal toxemia botulism, is a life-threatening disease caused by intestinal infection with Clostridium botulinum (Cb) spores. Infants are particularly susceptible to Cb infection because of their immature gut microbiota, whereas healthy adults are generally protected by gut microbiota-mediated colonization resistance. Thus, immature gut microbiota or gut dysbiosis is thought to permit Cb colonization. However, the mechanisms underlying

title: Sodium Butyrate: A Microbiota-Derived Short-Chain Fatty Acid Regulating Inflammation, Gut Barrier Function, and Colorectal Cancer Progression.
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a polyetiologic disease related to genetic changes, chronic inflammation, dysregulation of the intestinal barrier, diet and gut microbiota dysbiosis. Butyrate is a short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) produced by the microbiota that plays a crucial role in energy metabolism, epithelial homeostasis and mucosal immunity. title: Allicin attenuates diet-induced obesity in association with gut microbiota remodeling, fecal butyrate, and hepatic PPAR signaling in rats.
abstract: Obesity is associated with gut microbial dysbiosis and impaired intestinal barrier function. Allicin, a garlic-derived organosulfur compound, has shown anti-obesity effects, but the links between its effects on gut microbial metabolism and hepatic gene expression remain unclear. This study examined the metabolic effects of allicin and associated gut-liver responses using microbiota profiling, targeted short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) metabolomics, hepatic transcriptomics, network pharmacology and q

title: Microbiome-associated metabolites as emerging biomarkers of cancer immunotherapy response: from mechanistic networks to clinical validation.
abstract: Immune checkpoint blockade has improved outcomes across several cancers, yet many patients experience primary or acquired resistance. The gut microbiome may contribute to this variation through metabolic activities that influence systemic and tumor-associated immunity. This narrative review examines microbiome-associated metabolites as potential markers of immunotherapy response, with particular attention to their biological origins, immune effects, and clinical validation. title: Postbiotics derived from Latilactobacillus curvatus alleviate alcoholic liver injury by reshaping intestinal microbiota and activating the lysozyme-AHR-IL-22 axis.
abstract: Long-term alcohol exposure disrupts gut microbiota and mucosal immune homeostasis, promoting the pathogenesis of alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) via the gut-liver axis. Postbiotic intervention has emerged as a potential strategy for alleviating ALD, yet its protective mechanisms within the impaired intestinal microenvironment remain unclear. This study investigated whether postbiotics derived from Latilactobacillus curvatus can alleviate alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) and explored

title: Integrating untargeted and targeted metabolomics reveals how Bacillus amyloliquefaciens-Saccharomyces cerevisiae co-fermentation reshapes phenylpropanoid metabolism and enhances the prebiotic function of black rice.
abstract: Black rice is rich in anthocyanins and fiber, but its rigid bran limits nutrient release. A synergistic fermentation strategy using Bacillus amyloliquefaciens and Saccharomyces cerevisiae was employed to disrupt this barrier. Metabolomics revealed that fermentation reshaped phenylpropanoid pathways, boosting bioactive anthocyanins (24.83 mg/g) and antioxidant capacity (DPPH IC50: 0.0688 mg/mL). title: Multi-omics studies show that naringin improves cyclophosphamide-induced testicular and intestinal damage by enhancing energy metabolism.
abstract: Cyclophosphamide (CTX) is an anticancer agent that severely impairs male reproductive health. Naringin (NAR), a flavonoid compound, has the potential to ameliorate CTX-induced damage; however, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. In this study, an integrative approach combining transcriptomics, microbiome analysis, and serum metabolomics was employed to comprehensively evaluate the protective effects of NAR on reproductive function in CTX-treated mice. journal: The Journal of steroid biochemistry and molecular biology

title: Temporal and spatial dynamics and mechanisms of brain-gut axis injury induced by confinement-like physical restraint stress in mice.
abstract: Long-term SIS exposure across aerospace, deep-sea, underground, and quarantine settings increases depression and gut-brain axis dysfunction risk, but long-term nonlinear injury dynamics remain poorly understood.

title: Association of Blastocystis with the gut bacteria abundance and serum levels of serotonin in patients with irritable bowel syndrome; a case-control study.
abstract: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a chronic disorder of gut-brain axis. Although Blastocystis colonization has been reported in patients with IBS, the role of this parasite in modulation of the gut microbiota composition and the serotonin levels remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate association of Blastocystis colonization with serotonin-pathway-associated bacteria and serotonin levels in patients with IBS and healthy individuals. title: Beyond the brain: curcumin as a multi-target neuropharmacological modulator of the gut-brain axis in major depressive disorder and Parkinson's disease.
abstract: Curcumin, the principal polyphenol of Curcuma longa, has been proposed as a multi-target neuropharmacological agent for neuropsychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders. We propose that major depressive disorder (MDD) and Parkinson's disease (PD) share a convergent gut-brain axis dysfunction, and that curcumin can serve as a pharmacological probe to test whether this convergent pathway is causally relevant. title: Immunometabolic and epigenetic reprogramming in inflammatory bowel disease: from mechanistic circuits to therapeutic targeting.
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic, immune-mediated disorder of the gastrointestinal tract and an escalating global public health challenge, particularly in newly industrializing regions. Its etiology and pathogenesis remain incompletely understood, although disrupted homeostasis between the intestinal microbiota and the mucosal immune system is implicated. title: Children at risk of vitamin A deficiency exhibit taxonomic dysbiosis and functional remodeling of the gut microbiome: a matched case-control study.
abstract: Vitamin A deficiency is one of the most prevalent micronutrient deficiencies worldwide. This condition increases susceptibility to infections and due to its role in intestinal barrier integrity, it has been suggested that it could predispose to gut dysbiosis.

title: The (amide-)N-methylnicotinamide is a microbe-derived NAD+ precursor that drives gut stem cell renewal.
abstract: Nicotinamide Adenine Dinucleotide (NAD) is a critical cellular coenzyme whose decline associates with various chronic and inflammatory diseases. Improved NAD restoration may reduce disease risks and extend healthy lifespan. We report here that certain commensal bacteria including specific probiotic species produce (amide-)N-methylnicotinamide (N-MNA), which is a structural isomer of methylnicotinamide, a nicotinamide degradative metabolite. title: Study on Reconstruction of Functional Lactic Acid Bacteria Communities and on the Lipid Lowering Effect of their Fermented Lotus Leaf Beverage.
abstract: Hyperlipidemia, caused by dysregulated lipid metabolism, is closely associated with cardiovascular risk. This study developed a lipid-lowering beverage by fermenting lotus leaf (Nelumbo nucifera) extract with functional lactic acid bacteria (LAB). Three strains, Lactobacillus paracasei GY-L077, Lactiplantibacillus plantarum GY-L085, and Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus RB-01, were selected from traditional fermented foods for their antibacterial activity, gamma-aminobutyric acid production, lipase p

title: Comparative evaluation of edible Bifidobacterium species in repairing 5-fluorouracil induced intestinal microenvironment damage.
abstract: Chemotherapy-induced disruption of the intestinal microenvironment severely compromises both the quality of life and clinical prognosis of cancer patients. Despite the potential of edible Bifidobacterium to alleviate chemotherapy-associated intestinal damage, substantial inter-species comparisons remain to be clarified to support the rational selection of probiotic candidates. title: Effects of low-dose atorvastatin combined with reduced-dose prednisolone in acetic acid-induced ulcerative colitis in rats.
abstract: Long-term corticosteroid treatment for ulcerative colitis (UC) is often limited by dose-dependent adverse effects, highlighting the need for strategies that reduce steroid exposure. This study evaluated the efficacy of a combination of half-doses of Atorvastatin and Prednisolone in rats with acetic acid-induced colitis. title: High-carbohydrate and low-carbohydrate diets enriched in type II resistant starch from high-amylose maize influence cholesterol metabolism via concurrent alterations in fecal Bifidobacterium pseudolongum, bile salt hydrolase and bile acid profiles in mice.
abstract: This study investigated the impacts of high-carbohydrate (HC) and low-carbohydrate (LC) diets enriched in type II resistant starch from high-amylose maize (HAM-RS2) on circulating cholesterol concentrations and mechanisms linked to gut microbiota and bile acids. Compared to corn starch, HAM-RS2 resulted in lower plasma TC, LDL-C, and VLDL-C concentrations and adiposity, particularly in an HC context. title: Secondary bile acids disrupt hematopoietic stem cell homeostasis.
abstract: Gut microbiota dysbiosis caused by a high-fat diet disrupts hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) homeostasis; however, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we identify gut microbial secondary bile acid deoxycholic acid (DCA) as a key mediator of HSC dysfunction in mice. Plasma DCA levels were elevated during aging, consistent with previously reported increases in high-fat diet-fed mice. title: Fecal microbiome and plasma metabolome responses to Bacillus-based direct-fed microbial supplementation in cow-calf pairs from late gestation through weaning.
abstract: This study evaluated the effects of supplementation of a Bacillus-based direct-fed microbial (DFM) on the plasma metabolome and fecal microbiome of multiparous beef cow-calf pairs. On day 0 (94 ± 19 days prepartum), 296 Brangus crossbred beef cows were randomly assigned to treatments consisting of free-choice access to a trace mineral supplement alone (CON) or combined (BAC) with Bacillus subtilis 810 and B. licheniformis 809 (3 g/head/day; 6.6 × 109 CFU/head/day) from day 0 to 330 (weaning). title: Heat-inactivated Bifidobacterium adolescentis LA20 alleviates doxorubicin-induced senescence and barrier dysfunction in feline intestinal epithelial cells.
abstract: To investigate the protective effects and molecular mechanisms of heat-inactivated Bifidobacterium adolescentis LA-20 (HT-LA20) against doxorubicin (DOX)-induced senescent injury in feline intestinal epithelial cells (FIECs).

title: Hypoxia orchestrates the natural history of inflammatory bowel disease: Mechanisms and therapeutic opportunities.
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) arises from a dynamic interplay between epithelial dysfunction, immune activation, microbial dysbiosis and tissue remodelling. Although hypoxia was initially regarded as a consequence of intestinal inflammation, it is now recognized as an active regulator of epithelial, immune and stromal responses that coordinate disease progression. title: Targeting hormone conversion through dietary fiber improves polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome.
abstract: Excessive androgens serve as a primary driver for many phenotypic features of polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS). Although dietary fiber has been shown to alleviate PMOS, its effects on androgen concentrations and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. In a clinical trial, we demonstrated that a dietary fiber combination consisting of inulin, resistant starch, and β-glucan reduces androgen concentrations in patients' plasma. title: Microbial metabolism of methotrexate produces a STAT3 signaling molecule that alleviates gut inflammation.
abstract: Methotrexate (MTX) is a gold standard therapy for inflammatory diseases but has mixed therapeutic success in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). The gut microbiota impact MTX efficacy and toxicity by metabolizing MTX and altering its bioavailability, yet how inflammation alters this metabolism, and how the resulting metabolites act on the host, remain poorly understood. title: Dual Gut Microbiota-Dependent Mechanisms Underlying the Anti-Atherosclerotic Effect of Tilianin.
abstract: Tilianin (Til), a flavonoid from Dracocephalum moldavica L. and Agastache species, exerts potent anti-atherosclerotic effects via gut microbiota-mediated mechanisms. In atherosclerotic mice, Til dose-dependently reduced plaque burden and enhanced plaque stability by reducing necrotic cores and increasing collagen. title: Microbiota-derived indole-3-propionic acid regulates glucose homeostasis via remodeling of hepatic mitochondrial metabolism.
abstract: The gut microbiota produces metabolites that circulate to host tissues and are increasingly linked to metabolic health, yet the mechanisms by which individual microbial products regulate liver glucose metabolism remain poorly defined. Here, we identify the tryptophan-derived microbial metabolite indole-3-propionic acid (IPA) as a direct modulator of hepatic glucose production. title: β-glucan mitigates necrotizing enterocolitis-induced long-term cognitive impairment by remodeling gut microbiota and restoring tryptophan metabolite IAA-mediated gut-brain signaling.
abstract: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is a life-threatening gastrointestinal disorder prevalent in preterm infants, and most NEC survivors suffer from persistent cognitive deficits and neurodevelopmental disorders, with no targeted therapeutic approaches available to date. β-glucan has been documented to regulate gut microbiota, suppress inflammation, and exert neuroprotective effects, yet its efficacy and molecular mechanisms against NEC-associated cognitive dysfunction remain unclear. title: Gut microbiome depletion aggravates glial-mediated Alzheimer's disease pathology through inflammatory, metabolic, and proteostatic dysregulation.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by chronic neuroinflammation, metabolic dysfunction, and impaired proteostasis. Emerging evidence suggests that the gut microbiome influences brain function through the gut-brain axis; however, the mechanisms by which this communication affects AD pathology remain poorly understood. In this study, we used humanized Drosophila AD models expressing human AD-related transgenes in glial cells to investigate how glial

title: In vitro study of gut microbiota-mediated response to Salmonella Typhimurium with a focus on dynamics and immune modulation.
abstract: Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium is a major foodborne pathogen that disrupts gut microbial balance and induces intestinal inflammation. Microbial analysis revealed that S. Typhimurium infection increased the abundance of short-chain fatty acid (SCFA)-producing bacteria, including Bacteroides, Parabacteroides, and members of the Clostridia group, while decreasing Escherichia-Shigella in an in vitro fecal fermentation model. title: Enterococcus duransstrain AMA1 prohibiting free radicals, colon cancer and methicillin-resistantStaphylococcus aureus.
abstract: This research was conducted to determine bioactivity of ethyl acetate extract of our strain Enterococcus durans AMA1 that was previously isolated from bovine yoghurt. The study includes detecting of antimicrobial efficiency against Methicillin-Resistant S. aureus ATCC 33591 (MRSA), antibiofilm, antioxidant activity, anti-colon cancer activity and cytotoxicity. title: A putative model of the gut-muscle axis in aged livestock
abstract: The gut-muscle axis has been proposed to link gut microbiota with skeletal muscle physiology, yet its universality across livestock species remains unclear. Using aged laying hens, a livestock model with a relatively short digestive tract, we examined the gut microbiota, faecal metabolome, and breast-muscle metabolome by integrative multi-omics analyses in hens fed a Caldifermentibacillus hisashii-containing fermented feed or a control diet. title: Butyrate Deficiency due to Microbial Dysbiosis Promotes Anxiety.
abstract: Individuals with diabetes frequently suffer from anxiety; however, the mechanism for this association remains incompletely understood. Diabetes-associated genes have been implicated in the control of central nervous system (CNS) disorders. In the current study, we observed a marked down-regulation of secretagogin (SCGN) across multiple organs in diabetic mouse models, and Scgn knockout (Scgn -/-) mice developed diabetes, confirming SCGN as a diabetes-associated gene. title: The Microbiota-Metabolism Axis: Mechanistic Insights and Translational Targets Across Diabetes and Gastrointestinal Disorders.
abstract: The gut microbiota (GM) modulates host energy balance, glucose-lipid metabolism, and enteroendocrine signaling through metabolite-receptor axes that include short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) acting on FFAR2/FFAR3 (GPR43/GPR41), microbially transformed bile acids signaling via FXR/TGR5, and amino-acid/choline-derived compounds such as imidazole propionate (ImP) and trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO). title: Vitamin levels in consumers: is diet, dissolved vitamins or vitamins produced by gut microbiota the most important source?
abstract: Vitamins are continuously required for organismal metabolism. They are produced by phytoplankton, bacteria, and fungi and the general notion is that aquatic consumers, such as zooplankton and fish, obtain them from the diet. The focus here is on vitamin B1, called thiamine or thiamin, and the observation that concentrations of this vitamin decline with increasing trophic level. title: Microbiome-derived bile acids contribute to elevated antigenic response and bone erosion in rheumatoid arthritis
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic, disabling and incurable autoimmune disease. It has been widely recognized that gut microbial dysbiosis is an important contributor to the pathogenesis of RA, although distinct alterations in microbiota have been associated with this disease. Yet, the metabolites that mediate the impacts of the gut microbiome on RA are less well understood. title: Heat-killed Latilactobacillus sakei D279 Attenuates Lipopolysaccharide-Induced Intestinal Inflammation and Barrier Disruption
abstract: Intestinal barrier dysfunction and excessive inflammation contribute to the pathogenesis of various metabolic and gastrointestinal diseases. Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) induces systemic and intestinal inflammation, disrupts epithelial tight junctions, and impairs intestinal barrier integrity. Although heat-killed Latilactobacillus sakei D279 exhibits antiviral activity, its effects on intestinal barrier function remain unclear. title: Within-host evolution of an avirulent Salmonella vaccine strain reveals regulatory tuning of virulence functionality without loss of function
abstract: Non-typhoidal Salmonella (NTS) relies on a costly epithelial invasion program encoded in Salmonella pathogenicity island 1 (SPI-1) to overcome microbiota-mediated colonization resistance. Because SPI-1 expression is a cooperative trait in which a minority of invasive SPI-1ON cells benefits the wider bacterial population, inflammatory infection models readily select for permanently avirulent "cheater" mutants defective in SPI-1 function. title: Preclinical Development of Enterobacter ludwigii LS57, a Human-Derived Swarming Strain, as a Live Biotherapeutic Product for Inflammatory Bowel Disease
abstract: Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD) remains an area of major unmet need, and the undefined composition and manufacturing burden of fecal microbiota transplantation have motivated a shift toward single-strain Live Biotherapeutic Products (LBPs). Swarming bacteria are enriched in the stressed gut and limit mucosal damage, but no human-derived swarming strain has been developed as an LBP. title: Effect of Lactobacillus postbiotic supplementation on intestinal permeability, nutrient digestibility, and gut microbial and metabolic profiles in aging cats
abstract: Aging in cats is associated with declining nutrient digestibility and increased intestinal permeability, but evidence supporting microbiome-targeted interventions in older cats remains limited. We investigated whether daily supplementation with the Lactobacillus-derived postbiotic LB fermentate HF (LBHF) affected intestinal permeability, apparent total tract digestibility, gut microbiome composition, and fecal and plasma metabolomic profiles in older cats. title: Women's health outreach using a rapid and fieldable Nanopore-based microbiome profiling workflow.
abstract: Background In recent years, scientific interest in the vaginal microbiome has increased due to its impact on women's health. Colonization of the Lactobacillus species in the vagina may contribute to protection against vaginal infectious diseases. In order to create public awareness regarding vaginal health and to provide insights into the vaginal microbiome, a rapid field microbiome analysis using Nanopore sequencing was evaluated at Lowlands, a three-day music festival in the Netherlands. title: Characterization of Lactobacillus rhamnosus-Derived Extracellular Vesicles and Their Cellular Cytoprotective Effects Against Trimethylamine-Induced Oxidative Stress in Caco-2 Cells
abstract: Dietary trimethylamine (TMA) underwent gut microbiota-mediated catabolism and subsequent hepatic oxidation to generate trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO), a key metabolic factor linked to vascular and colorectal diseases. While the systemic effects of circulating TMAO were heavily investigated, the direct localized cellular interactions of its precursor, TMA, at the intestinal epithelial level required further elucidation. title: Metagenomic Insights into the Fecal Microbiome, Resistome, and Mobilome of Beef Cattle in Cow-Calf Operations in Florida, United States
abstract: Food-producing animals are a focus of One Health approaches to antimicrobial resistance (AMR) as reservoirs of antimicrobial-resistant bacteria (ARB) and antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs). We hypothesized that microbial composition, ARGs profiles, and mobile genetic element (MGE) profiles would differ by operation size and animal age group. title: Mucin promotes pneumococcal colonization via autolysis suppression and tryptophan-mediated immune modulation
abstract: Streptococcus pneumoniae is a leading human respiratory pathogen, yet its success depends not on disease but on its ability to persist as an asymptomatic colonizer of the nasopharynx. The nasopharyngeal mucosa is lined with mucus, whose heavily O-glycosylated mucin proteins are the most abundant macromolecules in the pneumococcal natural niche.
